issue.description:
Part of Phase 9 (docs/plan.md, '### First-Party Plugin Work', codex row). DEPENDS ON the envelope-unwrapping bead (bf-27p7) — do not start before it is closed.

The bundled plugins/codex.toml (v1.0) maps a flat {time, role, content} schema. Real ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl files use envelopes: line 1 is {type:"session_meta", payload:{id, cwd, cli_version, ...}}; subsequent lines are {timestamp, type:"response_item", payload:{type:"message", role, content:[{type:"input_text"|"output_text", text}]}} plus function_call / function_call_output payloads, {type:"turn_context", payload:{model}}, and event_msg noise. The current tests/fixtures/codex/*.jsonl are synthetic files matching the wrong mapping.

Work:
1. Rewrite plugins/codex.toml as v2.0 using [source.envelope]: payload_field="payload", type_field="type", type_routing { session_meta="meta", turn_context="meta", response_item="event", event_msg="skip" }. timestamp = "^timestamp". Project from session_meta payload cwd; model from turn_context/session_meta (DELETE the hardcoded static gpt-4).
2. src/parser/jsonl.rs event expansion for codex payloads (same pattern as the existing Claude Code tool_use expansion): payload.type=="message" → join content[] text blocks; "function_call" → tool_call event (tool name + args); "function_call_output" → tool_result event. Skip "reasoning" payloads.
3. Replace tests/fixtures/codex/rollout-*.jsonl with REAL-FORMAT fixtures (sanitized): one multi-turn session with a function_call/function_call_output pair, one minimal session. If a real ~/.codex/sessions tree exists on this machine, capture and sanitize from it; otherwise construct lines strictly following the schema above and note the provenance in a fixture README. Keep session_index.jsonl companion behavior working (src/scraper/companion.rs).
4. Integration test: scrape the fixture via the codex plugin end-to-end; assert event roles/order, project from cwd, model from turn_context, tool_call/tool_result pairing.

Acceptance criteria:
- agentscribe plugins validate plugins/codex.toml passes
- New fixtures parse to correct canonical events (asserted in tests)
- .jsonl.zst path still handled (open_file_maybe_zst)
- cargo test green, fmt + clippy clean
issue.title: Fix codex plugin: rewrite against real rollout format + real-format fixtures

issue.description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: /home/coding/AgentScribe/docs/plan.md

## Overview
AgentScribe is a Rust CLI binary that scrapes conversation logs from multiple coding agent types (Claude Code, Aider, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf), normalizes them into a canonical format, stores them as flat files with a Tantivy search index, and provides a query interface for agents seeking past solutions.

## Progress
- [x] Phase 1: Plugin System, Scraping & Normalization (agentscribe-mkg) — COMPLETE
- [x] Phase 2: Tantivy Indexing & Search (agentscribe-2dp.1) — COMPLETE
- [x] Phase 3: Enrichment & Intelligence (agentscribe-usx) — COMPLETE
- [x] Phase 4: Daemon Mode & MCP (agentscribe-slv) — COMPLETE
- [x] Phase 5: SQLite Format Support & Extended Agents (agentscribe-zef) — COMPLETE
- [x] Phase 6: Analytics, Knowledge Synthesis & Shell Integration (agentscribe-70w) — COMPLETE
- [x] Cross-Cutting: CI/CD, integration tests, release packaging, docs — COMPLETE
- [ ] Phase 7: Agent Integration & Session Export (agentscribe-p7x)
  - [ ] context subcommand — pre-task priming query (agentscribe-p7x.1)
  - [ ] render subcommand — individual session HTML export (agentscribe-p7x.2)

## Status
Phases 1-6 and all cross-cutting work complete. Phase 7 (NEEDLE integration + session export) in progress.

issue.description:
Split-child 1 of the json-array parser (parent: bf-459m).

The json-array format currently reads `items_path` from the WRONG place: `json_array.rs` pulls it out of `plugin.source.tree.session_glob` (piggybacking on the json-tree config), and the dedicated `JsonArrayConfig` struct is marked `#[expect(dead_code)]`. This child gives the format its own real config.

Scope:
- Add a proper source-array config to the `Source` struct in src/plugin.rs (e.g. `JsonArraySourceConfig { items_path: String }`), deserialized from an OPTIONAL `[source.array]` TOML table. `items_path` is a dot-path to the array within the document; "" or absent == document root.
- Update `JsonArrayParser` (src/parser/json_array.rs) to read `items_path` from the NEW `[source.array]` config in both `parse()` and `detect_sessions()`, replacing the `plugin.source.tree.session_glob` hack. Remove or repurpose the dead-code `JsonArrayConfig` stub.
- Verify/strengthen validation (src/plugin.rs ~line 432): json-array requires the same parser fields as jsonl (timestamp/role/content). Emit a clear `InvalidPlugin` error otherwise.
- Update the existing json_array.rs tests that currently build a `TreeConfig` to set `session_glob` to instead use the new `[source.array] items_path`.

Acceptance criteria:
- A plugin TOML with `[source.array] items_path = "data.messages"` parses and the parser navigates to that nested array; absent config defaults to root array.
- Validation rejects a json-array plugin missing required parser fields.
- The `source.tree.session_glob` hack is gone; `cargo build` is green and existing json-array unit tests pass.
issue.title: Add [source.array] config struct with items_path for json-array format

issue.description:
## Phase 2: Tantivy Indexing & Search

### Objectives
- Build Tantivy index from normalized sessions (BM25 scoring, faceted fields)
- Implement incremental indexing on scrape (no full rebuild required)
- Build three-tier tag extraction pipeline (explicit, structural, keyword list)
- Implement fuzzy search via Tantivy's Levenshtein term queries
- Implement "more like this" search via Tantivy's MoreLikeThisQuery
- Build context budget packing with greedy knapsack algorithm
- Implement structured JSON output mode for agent consumption

### CLI Commands
- `agentscribe index rebuild|stats|optimize` — manage the Tantivy search index
- `agentscribe search` — query interface (primary interface for agents)
- `agentscribe status` — show tracked agents, session counts, daemon state

### Tantivy Index Schema
See plan.md lines 347-391 for the full schema definition. Key fields:
- Full-text: `content`, `summary`, `solution_summary`, `code_content`
- Faceted: `session_id`, `source_agent`, `project`, `tags`, `outcome`, `error_fingerprint`, `file_paths`, `git_commits`, `doc_type`
- Code artifacts: `code_language`, `code_file_path`, `code_is_final`
- Date/numeric: `timestamp`, `turn_count`

### Tag Extraction Pipeline (Three-Tier)
1. **Explicit:** tool names from `tool_call` events (`Edit`, `Bash`, `Read`), languages from code fence markers (`` ```rust `` → `rust`)
2. **Structural:** file extensions from `file_paths` (`.rs` → `rust`, `.py` → `python`), command names from Bash content (`docker`, `git`, `npm`, `cargo`, `kubectl`), error types from `error_fingerprints`
3. **Keyword list:** match content against bundled technology dictionary (~200 terms: frameworks, databases, cloud services, protocols). Exact word-boundary matches only.

### Search Features
- Full-text BM25 search across session content and summaries (default mode)
- Error lookup: `--error <pattern>` against normalized error fingerprints
- Code search: `--code <query> [--lang <lang>]` for code artifacts
- Solution-only: `--solution-only` to return only extracted solutions
- Similar sessions: `--like <session-id>` using Tantivy MoreLikeThis
- Filters: `--agent`, `--project`, `--since`/`--before`, `--tag`, `--outcome`, `--type`, `--model`
- Output: `--max-results`, `--snippet-length`, `--token-budget <n>` (greedy knapsack)
- Structured: `--json` for agent consumption

### Content Truncation Policy
- `user` and `assistant` content: indexed in full
- `tool_call` content: indexed in full
- `tool_result` content: truncated to first 1000 chars per event
- Total document content capped at 500KB (trim middle if exceeded: keep first 250KB + last 250KB)

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tantivy index creation with full schema (all fields from plan.md)
- [ ] One document per session, concatenated with role prefixes
- [ ] Content truncation policy implemented (1000 chars for tool_result, 500KB total cap)
- [ ] Incremental indexing via `IndexWriter::add_document()` on scrape
- [ ] `agentscribe index rebuild` recreates index from session files
- [ ] `agentscribe index stats` shows document count, index size, segment info
- [ ] `agentscribe index optimize` compacts segments
- [ ] Three-tier tag extraction pipeline (explicit, structural, keyword list)
- [ ] Bundled technology keyword dictionary (~200 terms)
- [ ] Full-text BM25 search with default session-only results
- [ ] Fuzzy search via Levenshtein term queries
- [ ] `--like <session-id>` MoreLikeThis search
- [ ] `--error <pattern>` error fingerprint search
- [ ] `--code <query> [--lang <lang>]` code artifact search
- [ ] `--solution-only` filter
- [ ] All filter flags: `--agent`, `--project`, `--since`/`--before`, `--tag`, `--outcome`, `--type`, `--model`
- [ ] `--json` structured output mode
- [ ] `--token-budget <n>` greedy knapsack context packing
- [ ] `--max-results` and `--snippet-length` basic sizing
- [ ] `agentscribe status` command
- [ ] doc_type facet filtering (sessions vs code_artifacts, never mixed)

### References
- Plan: /home/coding/AgentScribe/docs/plan.md (lines 347-391 for index schema, lines 412-423 for phase scope, lines 465-510 for search interface)
- CLI reference: /home/coding/AgentScribe/docs/cli-reference.md
- Phase 1 bead: agentscribe-mkg
issue.title: Phase 2: Tantivy Indexing & Search

issue.description:
Reflection tooling needs to write back to AgentScribe. When a reflection tool analyzes sessions and determines 'this session's pattern led to a CLAUDE.md rule change,' it should record that annotation for future correlation.

## New: agentscribe annotate command

agentscribe annotate <session-id> --tag <tag> [--note <text>]

Examples:
  agentscribe annotate claude-code/abc123 --tag led-to-config-change --note 'Agent read CLAUDE.md then discovered missing rule'
  agentscribe annotate claude-code/abc123 --tag repeated-mistake --note 'Hit the br doctor corruption bug again'
  agentscribe annotate claude-code/abc123 --tag validated-rule --note 'Config rule: use sata not ssd was followed correctly'

Tags are free-form strings. Multiple tags per session allowed.

## Storage
Annotations stored as sidecar: ~/.agentscribe/sessions/<agent>/<session_id>.annotations.json
Format:
{
  session_id: string,
  annotations: [{
    tag: string,
    note: string | null,
    created_at: ISO8601,
    created_by: string  // 'human' | 'reflection-tool' | 'agentscribe'
  }]
}

## Query integration
- agentscribe search --tag <tag> — filter by annotation tag
- agentscribe reflect sessions now includes tags[] from both enrichment and annotations
- MCP tool agentscribe_annotate: add annotation to a session programmatically
  Input: {session_id, tag, note?, created_by?}
  Output: {ok: true}

## Programmatic use by reflection tools
The reflection tool (future) will call:
  agentscribe annotate <session_id> --tag <tag> --note '...'
or MCP agentscribe_annotate tool during its analysis run.

This creates a feedback loop:
  AgentScribe captures behavior -> reflection tool analyzes -> reflection tool annotates sessions -> future analysis can filter by annotation

## Acceptance Criteria
- agentscribe annotate command creates/appends sidecar JSON
- Multiple annotations per session supported
- agentscribe search --tag and agentscribe reflect sessions --tag filter correctly
- MCP agentscribe_annotate tool works
- Annotations survive re-scrape (stored as sidecars, not in beads.db)
issue.title: Session annotation write-back: tag sessions with reflection metadata

issue.description:
Split-child 2 of 4 for bf-27p7 (JSONL envelope unwrapping). Depends on child 1 (schema). Adds the routing dispatch that splits each JSONL line into event/meta/skip.

SCOPE (src/parser/jsonl.rs, in JsonlParser::parse_line):
- When plugin.source.envelope is Some: read type_field from the raw line, look up routing via envelope.get_routing().
- 'skip' -> drop the line (no event emitted).
- 'meta' -> route toward session-level metadata accumulation (project/model/version). Extraction detail may be light here, but the path must not crash and must not emit a spurious event.
- 'event' -> unwrap the payload_field object and treat it as the event body (payload_json) for downstream field mapping.
- Missing or non-object payload_field -> skip the line + emit a warning, NEVER panic (skip-and-log policy per Phase 1 plan).
- Set up envelope_json (full line) and payload_json (payload object) references so child 3 can wire field extraction to them.

NOTE: A partial dispatch skeleton already exists around the parse_line top (lines ~52-93) computing (_envelope_json, _payload_json). Complete the skip/meta/event handling and the missing-payload safety. Do NOT yet convert the timestamp/role/content/tool/tokens extractions to use payload_json — that is child 3.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- A fixture of enveloped lines routes correctly: skip lines dropped, event lines unwrap payload_field, meta lines do not emit events.
- A line whose payload_field is missing or not an object is skipped with a warning and no panic.
- No behavior change for plugins without [source.envelope] (payload_json == raw line).
- cargo test green; cargo fmt + clippy clean.

- Verify/extend scrape-state dedup (src/scraper/state.rs) so events already emitted for this file are not duplicated across rescrapes.
- Add code comments in json_array.rs AND the scraper explaining WHY byte offsets are unused and that dedup is intentional.

Acceptance criteria:
- Re-scraping an UNCHANGED json-array file emits nothing.
- Re-scraping after appending new items to the array emits ONLY the new events.

issue.description:
Observed on lab 2026-08-16: agentscribe daemon burned 36 CPU-min in 38 min wall (single thread at ~96%), re-parsing the NEEDLE fleet's live .jsonl transcripts from scratch on every append. Same files warned about 30-90x per 10 min (488 journal lines/10 min of identical 'Role field message.role not found' / timestamp warnings), driving journald to ~29% CPU average over 23h.

Fix, three parts:
1. Incremental parsing: track a per-file byte offset (persist in daemon state); on change events parse only appended lines instead of the whole file.
2. Warning dedup: emit a given warning class at most once per file (or rate-limit per file), not once per line per re-parse.
3. Debounce: skip files modified within the last few seconds and coalesce change events, so a streaming transcript is parsed in a few batches rather than per-append.

Interim containment already applied on lab (systemd drop-in ~/.config/systemd/user/agentscribe.service.d/limits.conf: CPUQuota=100%, CPUWeight=25, LogRateLimitIntervalSec=30/Burst=100) — that caps the damage but the daemon still wastes its whole quota; this bead removes the waste. Note the warning content itself likely relates to the envelope-unwrapping work (agentscr-6af48ff5) — fixing that removes these specific warnings, but incremental parse + dedup are still needed for any future parse warning on live files.
issue.title: Daemon: incremental transcript parsing + warning dedup (pegs a full core re-parsing live fleet transcripts)

Implement tier 3 (keyword dictionary matching) and integrate all three tiers into the document builder.

### Files to Create/Modify

issue.description:
daemon_state.json records `last_scrape` but nothing ever reads it back proactively. Confirmed live
on this box: the daemon has been dead and last_scrape has been stuck at 2026-06-24T13:14:19Z for
26 days (as of 2026-07-20) with nothing surfacing that fact short of manually reading a 43MB log
file. See docs/plan.md ADR-1 for full root-cause analysis (a corrupted scrape-state.json permanently
blocking the Scraper constructor).

Fix: `agentscribe daemon status` should compare `last_scrape` (and process liveness via the PID
file) against a threshold (e.g. > 2x the configured debounce/rediscovery interval, or a fixed
default like 1 hour) and print a clear WARN/CRITICAL line plus a non-zero-ish signal
(distinct exit code or a `"health": "stale"` field in `--json` output) instead of silently
reporting stale numbers as if everything were fine.

This is the single most impactful diagnostic fix from the audit: it would have caught the current
3+ week outage on day one instead of leaving it undiscovered until a manual filesystem inspection.

Depends on / references: docs/plan.md ADR-1 (root cause of the staleness this bead would surface).
File: src/cli.rs (daemon status command handler) and src/daemon.rs (daemon_state.json writer).
issue.title: Surface stale last_scrape as a warning in 'agentscribe daemon status'

## Linker Error Root Cause Identified

**Specific Linker Error**: `rust-lld: error: unable to find library -lcblas`

**Missing Symbol**: `cblas_sgemm` - BLAS (Basic Linear Algebra Subprograms) function used by turbovec for matrix operations

**Dependency Chain**:
- turbovec = "0.1" depends on: blas-src, faer, ndarray, openblas-src
- blas-src depends on: accelerate-src, openblas-src
- These require external C BLAS libraries to be present on the system

**Build Configuration Issue**:
- .cargo/config.toml had rustflags attempting to link BLAS libraries from Nix store paths:
  - `/nix/store/fwjsx7fqy3v4h8s3hxv74acrn5haspr-openblas-0.3.29/lib`
  - `/nix/store/ph7j87k0fp0ydci1nnkx9safl0lzhjg1-blas-3/lib`
- These Nix store paths are environment-specific and not portable

**Current State**:
- turbovec dependency commented out in Cargo.toml (line 60)
- BLAS linking flags commented out in .cargo/config.toml
- src/vector.rs is stub implementation - all turbovec usage already commented out

**Resolution** (Commits af5e6cb, 467331b):
- Commented out turbovec dependency to align Cargo.toml with stub implementation
- Commented out BLAS linking flags to prevent linker from attempting to link missing libraries
- Phase 8 semantic vector search remains non-functional stub until BLAS linking is resolved

**Next Steps** (for full Phase 8 restoration):
1. Resolve BLAS library linking - either use system BLAS or fix Nix store path approach

issue.description:
Implement `agentscribe render <session-id>` — renders a single archived session as a self-contained HTML file or structured Markdown for sharing and linking from commit messages.

## Motivation
Simon Willison publishes AI session transcripts as first-class versioned artifacts. AgentScribe has all the session data; it needs a render path to make individual sessions portable and shareable. The primary use case: `agentscribe render <id> --output /tmp/s.html && gh gist create /tmp/s.html` produces a permanent URL for a commit message.

## Interface
```
agentscribe render <session-id> [--output <path>] [--format html|markdown]
```
- `--output`: defaults to stdout
- `--format html`: self-contained HTML, inline CSS + JS, no CDN (default)
- `--format markdown`: alternating **User** / **Assistant** blocks with YAML frontmatter

## HTML output structure
```
<header>: project | agent | outcome | duration | models used | files touched
<conversation>: role badge + timestamp per turn; code blocks syntax-highlighted
<footer>: session ID | scraped at | "Generated by AgentScribe"
```

## CSS constraints
- Self-contained, inline, ~3KB budget
- Dark/light via `prefers-color-scheme`
- No external fonts — monospace stack only
- Code blocks: monospace, no external syntax CSS

## Syntax highlighting
- highlight.js subset: Rust, Python, TypeScript, Bash, YAML, TOML, JSON
- Embedded as `static str` constant (~50KB inlined JS)
- Full highlight.js is 500KB; subset sufficient for typical session content

## Markdown output
YAML frontmatter with metadata, then alternating fenced sections per turn. Code blocks fenced with language tags from original fence markers.

## Implementation
- New `Commands::Render` variant in `src/cli.rs`
- New `src/render.rs` with `render_html(session: &[Event], meta: &SessionMeta) -> String` and `render_markdown(...) -> String`
- highlight.js subset embedded as `const HLJS: &str = include_str!("../assets/hljs-subset.min.js")`
- New `assets/hljs-subset.min.js` (generate with highlight.js build tool, selecting 7 languages)
- ~300 lines of new code, no new Rust dependencies

## Tests
- `tests/render_tests.rs`: known session renders without panic, HTML output contains `<html>`, Markdown output contains frontmatter, unknown session ID returns error
issue.title: render subcommand — individual session HTML/Markdown export

   - Let `payload_json` = the value at `env.payload_field` inside the line (use extract_field); if that field is missing or not an object, fall back to `&json` so lookups still resolve via dot-notation through the payload_field path.
   - Apply type routing: read `env.type_field` from the line; if `env.get_routing(type_val)` == "skip", return Ok(Vec::new()) early (skip line); if == "meta", also skip for now (logging is out of scope); only "event" continues to normal field extraction.
2. When `plugin.source.envelope` is None: set both `envelope_json` and `payload_json` to `&json`, so all downstream behavior is unchanged.

Important: in THIS bead, do NOT yet swap the existing extract_string/parse_timestamp calls to the envelope-aware variants — only introduce the envelope_json/payload_json references and the early type-skip. Keep all current field lookups using `&json` exactly as today.

Acceptance criteria:
- A plugin with [source.envelope] whose line type routes to skip produces zero events (test with a pi/codex-style wrapped line).
- A plugin with no envelope config parses IDENTICALLY to before (existing test_parse_line_simple still passes; add a parity test asserting event fields are byte-for-byte unchanged).
- The include_types/exclude_types filters (which run before envelope resolution) are unaffected.
- cargo test passes.

issue.description:
The daemon's WatchLoop::try_watch (src/daemon.rs) logs `tracing::warn!("cannot watch directory")`
on every rediscovery cycle (default 60s) for any directory that fails to watch (e.g. permission
denied), forever, because failed dirs are never recorded anywhere on the Err branch.

Confirmed live on this box: ~/.agentscribe/daemon.log has been logging the identical WARN for
`/home/coding/.local/share/docker/volumes/<id>/_data` (root-owned, permission denied) once a
minute since the daemon's first-ever start on 2026-06-06 — tens of thousands of duplicate lines
contributing to an unbounded, unrotated log file.

Fix: track directories that failed to watch (e.g. a `failed_dirs: HashMap<PathBuf, Instant>` on
WatchLoop) and either skip retrying them entirely, or retry with real backoff and only log once
per backoff window, not once per 60s rediscovery cycle forever.

Ref: docs/plan.md ADR-1 (same audit that found this).
File: src/daemon.rs (WatchLoop::try_watch, around the "cannot watch directory" warn)
issue.title: Stop infinite identical WARN spam on unwatchable directories in daemon file watcher

issue.description:
Implement `agentscribe context "<task description>"` — a purpose-built pre-task query that returns a formatted, token-budget-packed context block ready for injection into an agent prompt.

## Motivation
`agentscribe search` is designed for humans typing keywords. Workers (NEEDLE, Claude Code, etc.) need a single call that returns a structured, injection-ready block combining past solutions + project conventions + file gotchas. This subcommand is that call.

## Interface
```
agentscribe context "<task description>" [--token-budget <n>] [--project <path>] [--json]
```
- `--token-budget`: default 3000. Applied globally across all three sections.
- `--project`: scope rules extraction to this path. Defaults to cwd.
- `--json`: wrap sections in a JSON object `{past_solutions, conventions, file_notes}` for programmatic assembly.

## Behavior
1. **Past solutions**: `execute_search(query=task_desc, solution_only=true, outcome=success, token_budget=budget*0.6)`
2. **Conventions**: inline rules extraction for `--project` (same pipeline as `agentscribe rules` but stdout not file)
3. **File notes**: parse task description for file path tokens, call `get_file_knowledge` for each, prepend gotchas

## Output format (default)
```
## Prior Context

### Past Solutions
[packed results]

### Project Conventions
[rules]

### File Notes
[per-file gotchas]
```

## Token budget semantics
Priority: past solutions > conventions > file notes. If budget exhausted, later sections omitted.

## NEEDLE integration point
In `NEEDLE/src/prompt/mod.rs`, `build_with_vars` context_parts assembly:
```rust
if let Ok(out) = std::process::Command::new("agentscribe")
    .args(["context", &bead.title, "--token-budget", "2000"])
    .output()
{
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout);
    if !text.trim().is_empty() {
        context_parts.push(format!("## Prior Context\n{}", text.trim()));
    }
}
```

## Implementation
- New `Commands::Context` variant in `src/cli.rs`
- New `context_pack` function in `src/search.rs` assembling the three sections
- Rules extraction needs a non-file output path (refactor `rules.rs` to return `String` instead of writing file)
- ~150 lines of new code, no new dependencies

## Tests
- `tests/context_tests.rs`: empty index returns empty output, non-empty index returns formatted block, token budget truncates correctly, `--json` output is valid JSON
issue.title: context subcommand — pre-task priming query for agent workers

Only consider extending the FormatParser trait if self-loading is infeasible.
- DELETE option: cost = remove src/parser/aider_input.rs, the AiderInputHistory import + parse_content_with_input_history + enrich_with_input_history + test_parse_aider_with_input_history from markdown.rs, and the `mod aider_input` + `pub use aider_input::{...}` from parser/mod.rs; add a CHANGELOG note. issue.description:
The reflection tooling that will auto-tune CLAUDE.md needs a clean, structured way to consume AgentScribe data — not just full-text search results. This bead adds a reflection-oriented export command and MCP tools.

## New CLI command: agentscribe reflect

### agentscribe reflect sessions [options]
Exports a structured JSON array of sessions with behavioral metadata suitable for reflection analysis.

Output per session:
{
  session_id: string,
  agent: string,
  project: string | null,
  started: ISO8601,
  ended: ISO8601 | null,
  duration_secs: int,
  outcome: 'success' | 'failure' | 'abandoned' | 'unknown',
  summary: string | null,
  tags: string[],
  model: string | null,
  tool_call_counts: {bash: int, read: int, edit: int, write: int, ...},
  re_read_count: int,
  bash_failure_count: int,
  read_config_files: string[],
  modified_config_files: string[],
  error_fingerprints: string[],
  anti_patterns: [{pattern: string}],
  files_touched: string[],
  config_changes_after: [{file: string, minutes_after: int}]
}

### Flags
--since <duration>      (e.g. 7d, 30d, 1y)
--project <path>        Filter by project
--outcome <success|failure|abandoned>
--modified-config       Only sessions where agent modified config files
--read-config           Only sessions where agent read config files  
--json                  Output JSON (default)
--csv                   Output CSV for spreadsheet analysis
--limit <n>             Max sessions (default 1000)

### agentscribe reflect patterns [options]
Cross-session behavioral pattern summary:
- Most common tool sequences preceding failures
- Files most frequently re-read before success
- Config files most frequently modified and what outcomes precede them
- Recurring error fingerprints and their resolution rates

## New MCP tools (add to src/mcp.rs)

### agentscribe_reflect_sessions
Same as CLI but MCP-shaped. Returns behavioral session list.
Input: {since_days: int, project: string?, outcome_filter: string?, modified_config_only: bool}

### agentscribe_behavioral_signals
Given a session_id, return full behavioral signals for that session.
Input: {session_id: string}
Output: full BehavioralSignals struct as JSON

## Implementation
- New src/reflect.rs module
- New Commands::Reflect variant in src/cli.rs with Reflect::Sessions and Reflect::Patterns subcommands
- Reads behavioral_signals.json sidecars (from bf-5t70) + search index
- Falls back gracefully when sidecars not yet built (runs enrichment on-demand)

## Acceptance Criteria
- agentscribe reflect sessions --since 7d --json outputs valid structured JSON
- agentscribe reflect sessions --modified-config filters correctly
- Two new MCP tools exposed and documented
- Output schema documented in docs/cli-reference.md as stable contract
issue.title: Reflection export API: structured behavioral data for reflection tooling

Read src/scraper/mod.rs to understand how paths flow through discover_files(), specifically:
- Where the outer glob iteration yields paths (line 247)
- How shellexpand produces expanded patterns
- Whether those paths are absolute or relative when passed to glob::Pattern::matches_path()
- Document the current behavior in the bead notes

issue.notes:
Path Flow Analysis through discover_files()

Key Locations:
- Line 344-347: Pattern expansion via shellexpand::full()
- Line 350-353: Glob iteration yields paths
- Line 256: Pattern.matches_path() call

Path Type Analysis:
Source Paths (after shellexpand): If pattern starts with ~ or /, yields absolute paths. If relative, yields paths relative to cwd.

Paths Yielded by glob(): Absolute patterns produce absolute paths (e.g. /home/user/.claude/**/*.jsonl yields /home/user/.claude/projects/session-123.jsonl). Relative patterns produce relative paths.

Current Behavior at Line 256: Paths from glob iteration are ABSOLUTE when source pattern starts with ~ or /. These absolute paths are passed to glob::Pattern::matches_path().

Pattern Normalization (Lines 369-378): Code normalizes relative exclude patterns to work with absolute paths by converting */subagents/* to **/subagents/*. This works because glob::Pattern::matches_path() supports matching relative patterns against absolute paths - the leading * or ** matches any number of leading path components.

Test Evidence: Lines 1775-1813 contain test_glob_pattern_relative_vs_absolute_matching() which proves relative pattern */subagents/* DOES match absolute paths by design.

Conclusion: No path handling inconsistency found. The system correctly expands ~ to absolute paths, yields absolute paths from glob iteration, normalizes relative exclude patterns, and leverages glob::Pattern's inherent support for relative-pattern-against-absolute-path matching.
issue.title: Investigate discover_files() path handling

issue.description:
The core signal for reflection tooling is: 'which agent behaviors preceded a config file change?' AgentScribe needs to detect when CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, memory files, or other agent config files are created/modified during or after a session.

## Problem
Git correlation (src/enrichment/git.rs) exists but:
1. Only looks at commits, not uncommitted edits
2. Does not specifically flag config/memory files vs code files
3. Does not correlate 'session happened, then config was changed within N hours'

## Two detection mechanisms needed

### 1. In-session detection (from tool_params - depends on bf-2a8w)
If a session's ToolCall events show Write/Edit calls to paths matching config file patterns, record these as 'config_writes' in BehavioralSignals (bf-5t70).
Patterns: **/CLAUDE.md, **/AGENTS.md, **/.claude/CLAUDE.md, **/memory/*.md, **/docs/notes/*.md, **/.needle/**, **/MEMORY.md

### 2. Post-session correlation (new: src/enrichment/config_change_tracker.rs)
Watch for config file changes at the filesystem level and correlate with recent sessions:
- After each scrape, scan for recently modified config files (mtime within last 24h)
- For each modified config file, find sessions that ended within 2h before the modification
- Record the correlation as an annotation: config_file_changed_after_session
- Store in: ~/.agentscribe/config-changes/<date>.json

## New: agentscribe config-changes command
agentscribe config-changes --since 7d
  Lists: config file, modification time, correlated session IDs, session outcomes

agentscribe config-changes --file CLAUDE.md
  History of all detected CLAUDE.md changes with correlated sessions

## MCP tool addition
New MCP tool: agentscribe_config_changes
  params: {since_days: int, file_pattern: string}
  returns: list of {config_file, modified_at, correlated_sessions: [{session_id, outcome, summary}]}

## Acceptance Criteria
- Config file changes detected and correlated with sessions
- agentscribe config-changes command works
- MCP tool exposed
- Patterns list configurable in config.toml: [reflection] config_file_patterns = [...]
issue.title: Config/memory file change detection: track when CLAUDE.md and similar files are modified

issue.description:
## Search Command Implementation

Implement the agentscribe search command — the primary query interface for agents and humans.

### Search Features
- Full-text BM25 search across session content and summaries (default mode)
- Fuzzy search via Tantivy Levenshtein term queries
- Error lookup: --error <pattern> against normalized error fingerprints
- Code search: --code <query> [--lang <lang>] for code artifacts
- Solution-only: --solution-only to return only extracted solutions
- Similar sessions: --like <session-id> using Tantivy MoreLikeThis

### Filter Flags
- --agent (source agent type)
- --project (project path)
- --since / --before (date range)
- --tag (extracted tags)
- --outcome (success/failure/abandoned/unknown)
- --type (doc_type: session or code_artifact)
- --model (model name)

### Output Modes
- Default: human-readable with snippets
- --json: structured JSON output for agent consumption
- --max-results N: limit result count
- --snippet-length N: control snippet size
- --token-budget N: greedy knapsack context packing (fit as many relevant results as possible within N tokens)

### Deliverables
- CLI subcommand in src/cli.rs
- src/search.rs module with query building, result formatting
- Greedy knapsack algorithm for --token-budget
- Unit tests for query construction and result formatting
- Integration test with a small test index

### References
- Plan: /home/coding/AgentScribe/docs/plan.md (lines 465-510)
- CLI reference: /home/coding/AgentScribe/docs/cli-reference.md
issue.title: Search command with BM25, filters, and output modes

- Read PID from ~/.agentscribe/agentscribe.pid
- Check if a process with that PID is actually running
- Handle stale PID files (daemon dead but PID file exists)
- Handle missing PID files (daemon never started or PID file deleted)

Acceptance criteria:
- Check reports PASS if daemon is running
- Check reports FAIL with clear message if PID file exists but process is dead
- Check reports FAIL if PID file is missing
- Works with both human and --json output formats

Phase 9 pi plugin (parent bf-4kv6). Depends on the schema-verification child.

The current fixtures (tests/fixtures/pi/multi-turn-with-tool.jsonl, edge-case-empty.jsonl, edge-case-truncated.jsonl) were authored against an unverified schema and may not match the real pi-mono format.

Work:
- Re-author each fixture to match the EXACT schema recorded in tests/fixtures/pi/README.md by the verification child: correct entry-type names, header fields (cwd/version/id), message role values, content-block shapes, tool-call and tool-result field names, and timestamp format.
- multi-turn-with-tool.jsonl: a complete multi-turn session with at least one assistant tool call and its matching tool result, demonstrating id/parentId ordering and tool pairing.
- edge-case-empty.jsonl: session header only (no message entries).
- edge-case-truncated.jsonl: header plus a partial/incomplete final line (simulating a mid-write crash).
- Keep fixtures synthetic but schema-accurate (no real PII); update the Fixtures section of the README to match.

Acceptance criteria:
- All three fixtures conform line-by-line to the verified schema in the README.
- The multi-turn fixture demonstrates a tool_call to tool_result pair matchable by id/toolCallId.
- Edge fixtures cover empty-session and truncated-write cases.
issue.title: Rewrite pi session fixtures to match verified schema

issue.description:
Claude Code stores subagent (spawned agent) sessions separately at:
  ~/.claude/projects/<path>/<session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl

The current claude-code.toml plugin EXCLUDES these via:
  exclude = ['*/subagents/*']

For the reflection use case, subagent behavior IS the behavior that matters most — NEEDLE workers are all subagents. Excluding them means AgentScribe misses the majority of actual agent work in a fleet environment.

## What to change

### plugins/claude-code.toml
Add a second source stanza (or remove the exclude and use session_id_from to differentiate):

Option A: Two source stanzas
[source]
paths = ['~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl']
exclude = ['*/subagents/*']
format = 'jsonl'
# ... existing ...

[[source.secondary]]
paths = ['~/.claude/projects/**/subagents/*.jsonl']
format = 'jsonl'
label = 'subagent'

[source.secondary.session_detection]
method = 'one-file-per-session'
session_id_from = 'filename'

[source.secondary.static]
source_agent = 'claude-code-subagent'

Option B: Parse isSidechain flag from events to distinguish
Add to [parser]: subagent_flag = 'isSidechain'
Set source_agent = 'claude-code' for isSidechain=false, 'claude-code-subagent' for true.

## Parent session linking
Subagent sessions should reference their parent:
- The parent session UUID is the grandparent directory name
- Add: parent_session_id: Option<String> to SessionManifest
- Populate from directory structure for subagent sessions

## Reflection relevance
With subagents captured:
- agentscribe reflect sessions shows fleet worker activity
- Behavioral signals (bf-5t70) apply to each worker session
- Can correlate: which worker session patterns lead to failures vs success
- anti_patterns on workers feed into CLAUDE.md improvements

## Acceptance Criteria
- Subagent JSONL files are scraped (not excluded)
- source_agent = 'claude-code-subagent' for subagent sessions
- parent_session_id populated where derivable from path
- agentscribe status shows claude-code-subagent sessions separately from claude-code sessions
- Existing tests still pass

issue.description:
Context: extract_with_envelope(path, payload, envelope) -> Option<Value> already exists in src/parser/mod.rs (lines 142-156) with full tests. But JsonlParser::parse_line uses extract_string (-> Option<String>) and parse_timestamp (-> Result<DateTime<Utc>>), which both call extract_field directly and have no envelope awareness.

Task: In src/parser/mod.rs, add two helper functions next to extract_with_envelope:
1. extract_string_with_envelope(path: &str, payload: &Value, envelope: Option<&Value>) -> Option<String> — routes through extract_with_envelope, then converts the resulting Value to String using the SAME rules as extract_string (String as-is, Number/Bool to_string, Null to empty string, other types None).
2. parse_timestamp_with_envelope(path: &str, payload: &Value, envelope: Option<&Value>) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> — routes the path lookup through extract_with_envelope to get the timestamp string, then applies the SAME parsing logic as parse_timestamp (RFC3339, epoch s/ms, bare UTC).

These are PURE ADDITIONS — do NOT modify parse_line or any existing function in this step. Mirror existing signatures exactly so the wrappers are drop-in candidates for the parse_line wiring in a later bead.

Acceptance criteria:
- Both functions compile and are exported from parser mod.
- Unit tests cover: ^field reads from envelope, plain field reads from payload, no-envelope (None) falls back to payload for plain fields and returns None/error for ^fields, dot-notation works, Number-as-timestamp parses.
- cargo test passes; no changes to existing tests or parse_line behavior.

## Cross-reference: bf-2brr investigation findings

Child 1 (bf-2brr) completed its read-only investigation. Key conclusions:

The premise that "aider_input.rs is referenced nowhere" was WRONG — markdown.rs already imports AiderInputHistory, exposes parse_content_with_input_history(), has a working enrich_with_input_history(), and a passing test (test_parse_aider_with_input_history) that asserts enriched per-message timestamps.

2. The actual gap is narrow: MarkdownParser's FormatParser::parse() trait impl (src/parser/markdown.rs:234) calls Self::parse_content() with hardcoded None instead of loading a sibling .aider.input.history file. The enrichment pipeline is fully wired — only the ~5 lines to discover+load the companion file are missing.

3. FormatParser::parse() signature is fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>> (src/parser/mod.rs:224) — no companion data mechanism in the trait.

4. Self-loading a sibling .aider.input.history inside MarkdownParser::parse() is fully feasible without changing the trait. source_path is available, and the load is best-effort (non-fatal if file absent).

See bf-2brr comment #4 for the full file:line details.

## Verified WIRE Decision from agentscr-638eccca

**Decision:** WIRE (not DELETE) — MarkdownParser self-discovers and loads sibling .aider.input.history

- MarkdownParser.parse() auto-discovers .aider.input.history as a sibling file
- Implementation: src/parser/markdown.rs:268 via Self::load_companion_input_history()
- Graceful degradation: missing/unreadable files return None, no error
- Conditional parsing: parse_content_with_input_history() when found, parse_content() otherwise
- Best-effort enrichment: timestamp precision improvement when companion exists

- All logic is contained within MarkdownParser implementation
- No changes to plugin TOML schema required

**Why NOT a contortion:** 
- Zero trait changes — entirely contained to MarkdownParser's internal implementation
- Self-discovery pattern is standard (mirrors existing session detection strategies)
- Graceful fallback makes it non-breaking for existing Aider installs
- No added complexity to scrape path — single optional companion lookup

issue.description:
Split from bf-2epr (decide fate of aider_input.rs). Decision-gate child. READ-ONLY: no code change.

VERIFIED CURRENT STATE: The wiring is already PARTIALLY done at the parser layer. src/parser/aider_input.rs (278 lines) is fully implemented (AiderInputHistory with find_timestamp_for_input, get_timestamp_by_sequence, load_from_file). src/parser/markdown.rs already has parse_content_with_input_history, enrich_with_input_history, and a direct unit test test_parse_aider_with_input_history that asserts enriched timestamps. So the parser-level wire path exists and works.

THE OPEN GAP: input history does NOT flow through the SCRAPE PATH. The FormatParser trait (src/parser/mod.rs around line 163) signature is fn parse(&self, source_path, plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>> with NO input-history parameter. MarkdownParser::parse (markdown.rs around line 234) calls Self::parse_content WITHOUT input history. So the scrape path never enriches timestamps today.

TASK: Decide WIRE vs DELETE and record the reasoning. Decision criterion from the parent: if it fits WITHOUT restructuring the FormatParser trait or adding scrape-path complexity, WIRE; otherwise DELETE.
- Investigate whether MarkdownParser::parse can auto-discover a sibling .aider.input.history file next to source_path and call parse_content_with_input_history WITHOUT changing the trait signature. If yes (expected), decision is WIRE.
- If auto-discovery would require changing the FormatParser trait signature or threading companion data through the scrape pipeline, decision is DELETE.

Acceptance criteria:
- A comment is added to this bead stating WIRE or DELETE with concrete reasoning that cites the FormatParser trait signature and names the chosen integration point (e.g. auto-discover sibling .aider.input.history inside MarkdownParser::parse, no trait change).
- No code change in this child. Do NOT implement here; that is child 2.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-12ko, 2026-07-07T00:30:49.742234075Z, author cli]
DECISION: WIRE.

Reasoning — auto-discovery of the sibling .aider.input.history requires NO change to the FormatParser trait and NO threading of companion data through the scrape pipeline:

1. TRAIT SIGNATURE (cited as required): src/parser/mod.rs:225 defines FormatParser::parse as fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>>. It already receives source_path, which is sufficient to derive the companion path locally inside the parser. No input-history parameter needs to be added to the trait.

2. INTEGRATION POINT (named as required): auto-discover the sibling INSIDE MarkdownParser::parse. Compute source_path.parent().join(".aider.input.history"), load it best-effort, and call parse_content_with_input_history(..., Some(history)). Fully self-contained in the parser — the scraper (src/scraper/mod.rs:495: parser.parse(file_path, plugin); LogFormat::Markdown -> MarkdownParser at mod.rs:459) is unaware and unchanged. No companion data is threaded through the scrape pipeline.

3. Graceful degradation: a missing/unreadable/empty companion returns None and parse() falls back to parse_content — no enrichment, no error, no added scrape-path complexity.

This meets the parent's decision criterion exactly (fits without restructuring the FormatParser trait or adding scrape-path complexity) -> WIRE, not DELETE.

Verification note: this decision-gate is read-only, and the wiring it authorizes is ALREADY present in the working tree (committed bf-2m3w / db5c521 'WIRE aider_input.rs — auto-discover companion .aider.input.history'). MarkdownParser::parse (markdown.rs:266-290) calls load_companion_input_history (markdown.rs:79-106) and routes to parse_content_with_input_history. So the scrape path DOES enrich Aider user-event timestamps today; the task preamble's 'OPEN GAP' was stale relative to the tree. No code change is required from this child.
issue.title: Investigate scrape-path integration and record wire-or-delete decision for aider_input.rs

Part of Phase 9 (docs/plan.md, '### Testing Strategy'). DEPENDS ON bf-2lns (codex fix), bf-1zpw (gemini-cli), bf-4kv6 (pi), bf-2h73 (goose), bf-2pcd (aider hardening) — all bundled plugins must exist in final form first.

Build tests/plugin_conformance.rs: one parameterized suite that runs over EVERY plugin TOML bundled in plugins/ (discover them at test time — adding a plugin must not require editing the suite, only adding fixtures).

For each bundled plugin (claude-code, aider, codex, opencode, cursor, windsurf, gemini-cli, pi, goose), assert:
1. VALIDATION: the TOML passes plugin validation (src/plugin.rs validate_plugin).
2. PARSE CORRECTNESS: its tests/fixtures/<plugin>/ fixture parses to an expected canonical event sequence — roles, event count, tool_call/tool_result pairing, project/model detection. Expected sequences live as small JSON/JSONL expectation files next to the fixtures (golden files), so failures show diffs.
3. MULTI-TURN RECONSTRUCTION: events come out in conversation order (timestamps monotonic or ordering-field order respected), across all session-detection strategies in use (one-file-per-session, delimiter for aider, per-item field for gemini-cli, sqlite rowid for cursor/windsurf).
4. INCREMENTAL TAILING: copy the fixture to a temp dir, scrape, append new events (format-appropriate: extra JSONL lines, extra markdown turns, extra array items, extra sqlite rows), scrape again — assert only the new events are emitted. For json-array and truncation_limit sources assert full-rescan correctness instead (no duplicates, no stale events). Use src/scraper/state.rs scrape-state in the temp dir.
5. EDGE CASES: each plugin has at least one malformed-input fixture (truncated line / bad JSON / empty session) and the scrape skips-and-logs without failing (skip-and-log policy, plan.md Phase 1).

A plugin missing fixtures = test FAILURE (forcing-function for future plugins). Cursor/windsurf sqlite fixtures: build the .vscdb in the test from SQL (rusqlite is already a dependency) rather than committing binary DBs, if no binary fixtures exist yet (check tests/fixtures/cursor, tests/fixtures/windsurf first).

Acceptance criteria:
- cargo test runs the conformance suite green for all 9 bundled plugins
- Removing a fixture dir makes the suite fail
- fmt + clippy clean
issue.title: Plugin conformance test suite: per-plugin fixtures, multi-turn ordering, incremental tailing

NEEDLE Phase 4 learning will call AgentScribe pre-dispatch: agentscribe search --error <fingerprint> --json and agentscribe search --anti-patterns --json. Both flags already exist (src/cli.rs: error: Option<String>, anti_patterns: bool). What is missing is a contract callers can build against.

Implement the Tantivy schema and index open/create logic. This is the first half of agentscribe-y71.

- Create `src/index.rs` — new module

- `pub fn build_schema() -> tantivy::schema::Schema` returning a schema with:
  - Full-text TEXT fields: `content`, `summary`, `solution_summary`, `code_content`
  - Faceted FACET fields: `session_id`, `source_agent`, `project`, `tags`, `outcome`, `error_fingerprint`, `file_paths`, `git_commits`, `doc_type`

[migrated comment from bf-2brr, 2026-07-04T17:54:58.593971130Z, author cli]
## Investigation findings — aider_input.rs usage and scrape path gap

### (a) What is already wired at the parser-unit level

src/parser/markdown.rs fully consumes AiderInputHistory:

- Line 6: use super::aider_input::AiderInputHistory;
- Line 26: parse_content() delegates to parse_content_with_input_history(content, ..., None)
- Lines 30-45: parse_content_with_input_history() accepts Option<&AiderInputHistory> and threads it to the inner parser
- Lines 51-73: Private enrich_with_input_history() matches user events to per-input timestamps via find_timestamp_for_input() (content-based) with sequence fallback
- Lines 85-91: parse_markdown_with_input_history() — the actual parse loop — applies enrichment at lines 224-227
- Lines 374-422: Test test_parse_aider_with_input_history already asserts enriched per-message timestamps (e.g., user_events[0].ts.timestamp() == 1773662430)

The enrichment pipeline is complete and tested. The only thing missing is the glue that loads the companion file.

### (b) Where the scrape path stops short

The scrape pipeline never touches aider_input at all:

1. src/scraper/mod.rs:415-421 — scrape_file() boxes a FormatParser from the LogFormat enum. For LogFormat::Markdown it creates Box::new(MarkdownParser).
2. src/scraper/mod.rs:445 — calls parser.parse(file_path, plugin) via the trait method.
3. src/parser/markdown.rs:234-248 — MarkdownParser's FormatParser::parse() impl reads the file content and calls Self::parse_content(content, ..., None) — hardcoded None, no attempt to discover or load a sibling .aider.input.history.

No code anywhere in the scrape path (src/scraper/mod.rs) constructs, loads, or passes an AiderInputHistory.

### (c) FormatParser::parse() trait signature

pub trait FormatParser {
    fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>>;
    fn detect_sessions(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>>;
}

(src/parser/mod.rs:222-228)

Takes only source_path and plugin. No mechanism to pass companion data.

### (d) Self-loading feasibility

Fully feasible without any trait signature change. Inside MarkdownParser::parse() (line 234), source_path is available. The impl could:

1. Derive a sibling path: source_path.parent().join(".aider.input.history")
2. Attempt AiderInputHistory::load_from_file() — if the file doesn't exist, return None (non-fatal)
3. Call Self::parse_content_with_input_history(content, ..., Some(&history)) instead of Self::parse_content(content, ..., None)

All of this is internal to MarkdownParser's trait impl. The FormatParser::parse() signature remains unchanged. The parse_content_with_input_history / enrich_with_input_history / find_timestamp_for_input plumbing already exists and is tested. The only missing piece is ~5 lines inside the trait impl to discover and load the sibling file.
issue.title: Re-verify current aider_input.rs usage and resolve stale premise

Implement the long-running daemon for continuous scraping and optional MCP server.

## Deliverables

### Daemon Core
- `agentscribe daemon start|stop|status|run|logs` commands

- Scrape debounce (default 5s) to avoid thrashing during active sessions
- Incremental index updates (no full rebuild per session)
- PID file management (~/.agentscribe/agentscribe.pid)
- Log file (~/.agentscribe/daemon.log)
- Files: src/daemon/mod.rs, src/daemon/watcher.rs, src/cli/daemon.rs

### MCP Server (Optional)
- Unix socket MCP server at ~/.agentscribe/mcp.sock
- Four tools: agentscribe_search, agentscribe_status, agentscribe_blame, agentscribe_file
- All tools call same core library as CLI
- Config toggle: [daemon] mcp_enabled = false
- Files: src/mcp/mod.rs, src/mcp/tools.rs

### Systemd Integration
- Generate systemd user-level service unit file
- `agentscribe daemon install` to create ~/.config/systemd/user/agentscribe.service
- Files: src/daemon/systemd.rs

## Testing
- Integration test: daemon watches a directory, detects new file, scrapes automatically
- Test debounce: rapid file changes produce single scrape
- Test MCP tools return same results as CLI equivalents
- Test daemon graceful shutdown (SIGTERM)

## Acceptance Criteria
- `agentscribe daemon start` runs in background, watches all plugin source paths
- New agent log files are automatically scraped within debounce window
- `agentscribe daemon status` shows PID, uptime, RSS, last scrape time
- MCP server (when enabled) responds to all four tool calls correctly
- Daemon RSS stays under 20MB when idle

`RollingFileAppender` with daily or size-based rolling and a retention count), or add a
config.toml option (e.g. `[daemon] log_max_bytes`) that truncates/rotates when exceeded.

Ref: docs/plan.md ADR-1 (same audit that found this — mentioned in ADR-1's "Follow-up work required").
File: wherever the tracing subscriber/file writer is configured for daemon mode (search for the
daemon.log path construction in src/daemon.rs / src/main.rs).

issue.description:
StateManager (src/scraper/state.rs) persists ALL tracked source-file offsets as one JSON document
that gets fully re-serialized and rewritten (under an exclusive flock) on every single incremental
update via `update_file_state`. Confirmed live on this box: the file is already 4MB for ~21.5K
tracked sources after a few months of use, and docs/plan.md's own Phase 8 sizing section targets up
to ~500K sessions — full-document rewrite-on-every-update will not scale to that target (write
amplification + lock hold time grows with corpus size, not with the size of the actual update).

This is the long-term follow-up named in docs/plan.md ADR-1 ("Alternatives Considered" and
"Consequences" sections) — ADR-1 itself only makes the current JSON-file approach crash-safe
(atomic write + quarantine-on-corruption), it does not change the O(n) rewrite cost.

Fix direction: replace the single JSON file with a keyed embedded store (`sled`, `redb`, or a small
SQLite table keyed by source file path) so `update_file_state` for one file touches only that file's
row/key, not the whole corpus. Preserve the existing `StateManager` public API (get_file_state,
update_file_state, set_offset, etc.) so scraper/mod.rs and daemon.rs don't need to change.

Depends on: docs/plan.md ADR-1 (do the crash-safety fix first; this is the scale follow-up).
File: src/scraper/state.rs
issue.title: Move scrape-state persistence from full-file JSON rewrite to a keyed store (O(1) incremental updates)

issue.description:
Auditing this box's live ~/.agentscribe/ data directory by hand (as part of a fleet-wide artifact
review, 2026-07-20) surfaced multiple problems that a single diagnostic command could have caught
in seconds instead of requiring manual filesystem/log inspection:

- daemon process dead (stale PID in agentscribe.pid) with no scraping for 26 days
- scrape-state.json corrupted (state file error) — see docs/plan.md ADR-1
- daemon_state.json's `sessions_indexed` count present but no index/ directory actually on disk
  (IndexManager::open can fail silently — best-effort, see src/scraper/mod.rs Scraper::new_with_lock_timeout)
- mcp_enabled=false even though the MCP server is the tool's flagship "agents query their own
  history" feature (README "MCP Server" section)

Proposal: a new `agentscribe doctor` CLI subcommand that checks, in one pass:
1. Is the daemon process alive (PID file vs actual process)?
2. Is `last_scrape` recent relative to the debounce/rediscovery config?
3. Does state/scrape-state.json parse cleanly?
4. Does index/tantivy/ exist and is its doc count roughly consistent with sessions/ file count?
5. Is mcp_enabled set, and if so is the socket path reachable?

Print a pass/fail summary per check (similar spirit to `cargo doctor`/`brew doctor`), with
`--json` output for scripting/monitoring.

This overlaps with and can share plumbing with the narrower "surface stale last_scrape in daemon
status" bead — doctor is the broader one-shot diagnostic, daemon status's staleness warning is the
always-on version of check #2 specifically.

References: docs/plan.md ADR-1.
File: new subcommand in src/cli.rs.
issue.title: Add 'agentscribe doctor' command to self-diagnose the exact failure modes found in this audit

issue.description:
The current Event schema captures tool calls with tool: Option<String> and content: String. For reflection tooling (analyze agent behavior -> improve CLAUDE.md), we need structured extraction of tool call parameters.

## Gap
- Cannot query 'what bash commands were run' or 'what files were read vs written' without parsing the raw content string
- tool_params is currently not extracted or stored
- File paths appear in file_paths[] but without context (was it a Read or an Edit?)

## Implementation

### Extend Event schema (src/event.rs)
Add optional field: pub tool_params: Option<serde_json::Value>
Backward-compatible: absent = None on deserialize.

### New src/enrichment/tool_params.rs
For Claude Code ToolCall events, content is JSON. Extract per known tool:
- Bash: {command: '...'} -> store as-is
- Read: {file_path: '...'} -> store as-is
- Edit: {file_path, old_string, new_string} -> store (truncate strings to 200 chars for index)
- Write: {file_path, content} -> store (truncate content)
- MCP tool calls: {tool_name, params} -> store

For ToolResult events: extract exit_code or error flag if present in JSON content.
Fall back gracefully for non-JSON content (Aider, Markdown-format agents).

### Index extension (src/index.rs)
Add tool_params_json as STORED field (not indexed for BM25, just stored for retrieval).

## Acceptance Criteria
- event.tool_params populated for Claude Code ToolCall events
- Bash commands extractable: event.tool_params['command']
- File paths from Read/Edit/Write in both file_paths[] and tool_params
- Tests in src/enrichment/tool_params.rs for each known tool type
- Existing tests still pass

issue.description:
Split-child 2 of the json-array parser (parent: bf-459m). Depends on split-child 1.

The per-object -> Event mapping (timestamp parse, role + role_map, content, tool_name, tokens_in/out, project field detection, static_fields) is currently DUPLICATED between `JsonlParser::parse_line` (src/parser/jsonl.rs) and `JsonArrayParser::parse_item` (src/parser/json_array.rs). The parent bead explicitly requires reuse, not duplication.

Scope:
- Factor the shared per-object mapping into a single helper (e.g. a free function `map_object_to_event(value, context, plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>>` in src/parser/mod.rs, or a small shared module) that both parsers call.
- Refactor `JsonlParser` to route each line's parsed JSON object through the shared helper.
- Refactor `JsonArrayParser::parse_item` to call the same helper, deleting the duplicated body.
- Preserve include_types/exclude_types filtering and skippable-error (skip-and-log) semantics for both.

Acceptance criteria:
- jsonl parsing behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (all existing jsonl tests pass unchanged).
- json-array emits identical events before and after the refactor.
- No duplicated mapping logic remains across the two parsers; `cargo test` green.
issue.title: Factor shared per-object field mapping out of jsonl.rs for reuse
